body:
Genuinely a nitpick, but we have them now, so-
```suggestion
			The node's execution order of the process callbacks ([method _process], [constant NOTIFICATION_PROCESS], and [constant NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PROCESS]). Nodes whose priority value is [i]lower[/i] call their process callbacks first, regardless of tree order. This value must be set between [member @GlobalScope.INT32_MIN] and [member @GlobalScope.INT32_MAX].
```
Not as easily as "letting the Inspector know" because unfortunately the underlying method signature is unknown to the binding side of things...

That would make sense, since a lot of properties are `int` rather than `int64_t` or `uint64_t` after all. This would effectively make this PR obsolete too.

That said, does ClassDB keep track of the original C++ type used for each property (without coalescing both `int` and `int64_t` into `Variant::INT`)?
It doesn't, but it could theoretically keep track of the "sub-type" as a type hint, like how enums are `int64` under the hood but still show up in the editor as enums.
